Vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, no fr: Vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, no frameworks or dependencies. The app stays small and fast on low-end phones and slow connections. There's no build step and nothing third-party to break or review. No backend. Data lives in the browser's local storage. This protects privacy and removes server costs. The trade-off is that data doesn't sync across devices, so I added backup and restore. Money stored as integer cents. This prevents the rounding errors that floating-point numbers cause when adding tax and discounts. Ethiopian calendar written from scratch using Julian Day Numbers, instead of a library. I could handle leap years and test the conversions myself. Print-to-PDF through the browser's print engine instead of a PDF library. Many libraries render Ge'ez script badly, and the browser's engine handles it correctly. Service worker with network-first caching. The app works offline, but users still get new versions right after an update. Static hosting on Vercel. There's nothing to run on a server, so the site is fast and cheap to host.
